name: MPU-6050
description: 6-axis MEMS motion tracking device combining a 3-axis gyroscope and a 3-axis accelerometer on one die, with an on-chip Digital Motion Processor (DMP). It communicates over I2C (up to 400 kHz) and includes a 1024-byte FIFO and a 16-bit ADC per channel. The popular GY-521 breakout adds a 3.3 V LDO and I2C pull-ups so it can run from 5 V. An auxiliary I2C master bus (XDA/XCL) lets it read an external magnetometer for a 9-axis solution.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: supply; GY-521 has an onboard 3.3 V regulator so accepts 3.3-5 V (the MPU-6050 chip VDD is 2.375-3.46 V)

pins.name: XDA
pins.description: auxiliary I2C master data (to external sensor e.g. magnetometer)

pins.name: XCL
pins.description: auxiliary I2C master clock (to external sensor)

pins.name: AD0
pins.description: I2C address LSB select: low = 0x68, high = 0x69

pins.name: INT
pins.description: interrupt output (data ready, FIFO, motion detect)

typical_application: Tilt/orientation sensing, drones and gimbals, gesture and motion detection, self-balancing robots, fused with a magnetometer for AHRS/9-DOF.
gotchas: the bare MPU-6050 chip is a 3.3 V part (VDD max 3.46 V); only the GY-521 board's onboard LDO makes 5 V safe - never feed 5 V to the raw chip VDD
AD0 sets the 7-bit I2C address: 0x68 when low (default, often pulled low on the board), 0x69 when high
XDA/XCL are the auxiliary master bus for an external magnetometer, not extra I2C for the host - leave unconnected if unused
I2C logic on the bare chip is referenced to VLOGIC; some clones tie it to VDD so 5 V I2C logic can be out of spec
many cheap clones use a lower-grade die and show more gyro drift; allow warm-up and calibration
largely superseded (MPU-6500/ICM-series) but remains the canonical hobby IMU
